model: Regulated utility dividend capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route)

inputs.base_revenue_note: NOT sales. The engine's 'revenue' line is earnings attributable to common on the current fully diluted count: FY2026E diluted EPS $5.15 (midpoint of the $5.05-5.25 guidance raised on 2026-11-03; nine-month actual is $5.20) x 128.8M shares = $663.3M. Growth rates are PER-SHARE EPS growth from FY2027, so the dilution from the equity that funds the capital plan is already inside the path. Value per share is independent of the share count on this route (the count scales numerator and divisor alike).
inputs.share_count_basis: 121.20M shares outstanding at 2026-10-28 (Q3-2026 10-Q cover) + 6.63M forward-sale shares that mature by February 2027 (4.43M left on the February 2024 forwards due 2026-12-31, 0.55M 2024-ATM and 1.65M 2025-ATM forwards) + ~0.5M performance shares/RSUs + ~0.47M convertible-note excess shares (diluted EPS table, Q3-2026) = ~128.8M. A further 8.45M 2026-ATM forward shares (maturing July 2027 - September 2028, ~$842M) plus a $90M October 2026 forward are future plan funding and are charged once, through per-share EPS growth, not through the divisor. Held FLAT.
inputs.net_debt_note: Held at zero by construction: the flow is dividends to common, which are after interest, NCI and reinvestment. Deducting the $11.4B of debt again would count it twice. Actual balance sheet at 2026-09-30 is in total_debt and cash.
inputs.total_debt_note: Short-term borrowings 438.6 + current maturities 825.0 (includes the $525M 4.75% convertible notes due June 2027) + long-term debt 10,164.4, Q3-2026 10-Q consolidated balance sheet. Metrics.csv total_debt (10,989.4) excludes short-term borrowings.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 XBRL cash-flow add-back (Metrics.csv StockBasedComp). No combined adjusted-EBITDA figure is published. SBC is already an expense inside EPS, so the forward sbc_pct_path is 0 on this route and house and street bases coincide (band_position not meaningful).
inputs.wacc_rationale: The discount rate is a COST OF EQUITY, not a WACC, because the flow is post-interest. USD build: 10-year US Treasury 5.15% (Yahoo ^TNX, 2026-11-13) + beta 0.65 x 4.75% ERP = 8.25%, the same build used for NI so regulated-utility values are comparable. Same rate in all three scenarios; rate-case, single-regulator and large-load risk are carried by the scenario paths and weights, not by a rate premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable on this route: lease cost (mostly purchased-power agreements accounted as leases, $3.7B of lease liabilities at FY2025) is inside net income and largely recovered through the fuel adjustor; net debt is not deducted.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the flow: EPS is after net income attributable to the Palo Verde sale-leaseback VIE ($6.6M in 9M-2026). No NCI deduction in the bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE. Pinnacle West is a single-subsidiary, cost-of-service regulated electric utility (APS, Arizona) in a capex supercycle ($2.6-2.7B a year of APS capex against ~$2.0B of EBITDA, rate base guided to grow 7-9% through 2028). The dcf-methods routing table has no utility row; its governing principle is to discount the flow the business actually produces at the rate appropriate to whom it accrues, and it warns that reported FCF is structurally negative for infrastructure in a capex supercycle without that being a signal. Reported FCF has been negative every year since FY2019 (FY2025 -$820M, owner FCF -$847M after SBC) because rate base is being grown on purpose, so an unlevered owner-FCF DCF would rest entirely on a terminal value after a guessed capex normalisation, less $11.4B of debt. The flow that reaches shareholders is the dividend, funded by authorised returns on equity rate base, so the model capitalises dividends per share at the cost of equity through the Drivers engine with net debt at zero, the same route used for NI, PEG, PCG and NEE. ENGINE MAPPING: 'revenue' = earnings to common (per-share EPS x flat current share count); ebitda_margin 100%; capex_pct = earnings retention (100 - payout); D&A, tax, SBC and working capital 0 because EPS is already after all of them; FCF = dividends. Year 1 is FY2027; FY2026 dividends are mostly paid and are excluded. Terminal payout of 68% with 3.0% growth is consistent with g = retention x ROE at an earned ROE of 8.5-9.5% (FY2026E EPS $5.15 on $61.71 book = 8.3%; APS authorised 9.55%, requested 10.70%). last_fcf is recorded as true owner FCF (-819.5 - 27.5) for auditability and is NOT the base of this model. Price is a regular-session close, not an after-hours print. No buybacks (treasury purchases are tax-withholding only); Pinnacle West is a net issuer of equity (forward sales and a $500M 2026 ATM program). Unrecognised upside not modelled: $35-40M a year of Nuclear PTC claimed on tax returns but held as an uncertain tax position pending IRS guidance and an open 2022-2024 exam.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: management per-share EPS guidance (FY2026 $5.05-5.25; 5-7% long-term CAGR through 2030 off the 2024 base), haircut to the lower half; not a historical CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (4.8% 3yr / 4.3% 5yr) diverges more than 30% from the revenue CAGR (7.3% / 8.3%) and from the 5yr EPS CAGR (0.7%). Revenue is inflated by pass-through fuel and purchased-power costs; the 5yr EPS figure is depressed by the adverse 2019 rate-case decision that cut FY2022 EPS to $4.26. Book equity growth (4-5%, after a ~70% payout plus issuance) is the closest historical read on per-share compounding and sits just below the selected 5.5%.
historical_growth.notes: FY2020-FY2025 annual figures from Metrics.csv. FCF CAGRs undefined: owner FCF (reported FCF less SBC) is negative in every year of the window (FY2022 -482, FY2023 -656, FY2024 -663, FY2025 -847), which is the capex program, not distress. DPS has grown only ~1.7% a year (3.52 -> 3.58 -> 3.64) as management works the payout down into its 65-75% target.

base.growth_note: Per-share EPS, FY2027-FY2036. FY2027 +4.5% to $5.38: new base rates from the 2025 rate case partly offset by weather normalising (2026 carried a ~$56M pre-tax weather benefit year on year through nine months), settlement of ~6.6M forward shares and higher interest. FY2028-FY2030 at 6.5/6.5/6.0%, giving FY2030E $6.47, between the 5% and 6% lines of the 5-7% guide off the 2024 base. Fades to 3.5% by FY2035 as the large-load queue is absorbed.
base.capex_note: capex_pct is earnings retention = 100 - dividend payout. Payout 69% in FY2027 (DPS ~$3.71 against the current $3.64 rate), drifting to 65% (the bottom of the 65-75% target) while the build peaks and DPS growth lags EPS as it has since 2022, then back to 68% as growth slows.
base.terminal_note: Gordon at 8.25% / 3.0% = 19.6x terminal dividend, about 13.3x earnings. The cap is on the dividend flow: 28x dividends = ~19x earnings at a 68% payout. Gordon binds.

bull.growth_note: FY2026 lands at $5.25 (top of range) and FY2027 at $5.62 (+7%), which is +9.1% on the $5.15 base; then 8% through FY2029, giving FY2030E ~$7.05, the 7% line of the guide. Payout at 63-66% while the build is at its peak.

bear.growth_note: FY2026 lands at $5.05 (bottom of range) and FY2027 at ~$5.10: an adverse rate-case order (no formula rate, ROE held near 9.55%, a data-center rate design that shifts cost to shareholders) leaves regulatory lag in place while weather normalises and forward shares settle. Growth then runs at 3.5-4%, below the 5% floor of guidance, and decays to 2.5%. The dividend is held with token raises; payout stays 70-72%.

scenario_narratives.base: The outgoing all-Republican ACC decides the 2025 rate case around December 2026 with a meaningful but trimmed increase and some form of lag relief, and APS keeps spending $2.6-2.7B a year into a rate base growing 7-9%. Large-load customers (TSMC, data centers in the 5.8 GW committed queue) ramp roughly on schedule and pay for their own infrastructure under the subscription model, so weather-normalised sales grow 5-7%. Per-share EPS compounds about 6% a year from the raised 2026 level to 2030, in the lower half of the 5-7% target, because the plan needs roughly $1B of forward equity over two years and debt is refinanced at higher coupons. The dividend grows more slowly than earnings as the payout is worked down to 65%. After 2032 Pinnacle West is an ordinary rate-base compounder growing 3% with a 68% payout.
scenario_narratives.bull: Arizona stays the preferred corridor for semiconductor and data-center siting, a slice of the ~20 GW uncommitted queue converts into contracted load on direct-pricing terms, and the ACC adopts the formula rate adjustment mechanism so capex is recovered with little lag. The 2026 guidance raise proves to be a step-up rather than a pull-forward, per-share EPS tracks the top of the 5-7% range to 2030 and stays above 6% into the early 2030s, and the Nuclear PTC position is resolved in the company's favour. The larger asset base supports 3.5% growth afterwards.
scenario_narratives.bear: The single-regulator risk shows up. The rate-case order rejects the formula rate, trims the return and loads data-center infrastructure risk onto APS; from January 2027 a 3-2 commission with two new consumer-focused members makes every later case harder, as the 2019 case did when it cut FY2022 EPS by 22%. At the same time an AI-capex slowdown delays large-load ramps after the generation and transmission is committed, and the equity layer is defended with more forward sales at lower prices. Wildfire liability and Colorado River water constraints are the tail behind this case. Pinnacle West remains a solvent regulated utility that holds its dividend; it stops being a growth story.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: one regulator sets essentially all earnings, a contested rate case is weeks from decision, the commission's composition changes in January 2027, and this regulator has delivered a punitive order within the last five years. Base 50%: guidance is specific, was raised twice in 2026 and rests on contracted load. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs formula-rate adoption, uncommitted queue conversion and on-budget construction together, and the stock already prices growth above guidance.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Pinnacle West is valued as what a shareholder receives: a dividend funded by regulated earnings on APS's rate base, growing with per-share EPS, capitalised at an 8.25% cost of equity. Dilution from the equity-funded capital plan is charged once, through per-share growth. The franchise makes the dividend durable; the question the model answers is how much to pay for large-load growth when the 10-year Treasury yields 5.15%, the dividend yields 3.4% and the stock trades at about 21x FY2026E earnings and 1.7x book.
key_risks_to_valuation: Discount-rate sensitivity is the largest lever: the stream is long-duration and the terminal value is most of the value, so each 0.5pt on the cost of equity moves the result by roughly 10%. A fall in long rates would lift the value materially.

The 2025 rate-case decision (expected around December 2026) lands after this valuation and moves FY2027 EPS directly; the three year-1 growth rates bracket it and should be re-judged when the order is issued.

FY0 is the FY2026 guidance midpoint ($5.15), not an audited year. Nine-month EPS is already $5.20, so the midpoint implies a small Q4 loss; Q4 has ranged from about -$0.04 to +$0.12 in the last two years.

EPS guidance, the 5-7% growth target and the payout target come from earnings materials summarised in the Analysis JSON, not from the 10-K/10-Q text; share count, forwards, debt and dividends declared are from the Q3-2026 10-Q.

Exit multiple: Gordon at the cost of equity gives roughly 13x terminal earnings against about 21x today. The model assumes multiple compression as growth normalises; holding today's multiple would roughly close the gap to the market price.

A 15% hurdle is far above what a regulated utility earning ~9.5% on equity can deliver at any price near book; the entry price is a statement about the hurdle, not a forecast that the stock will trade there.
House and street bases coincide on this route because SBC is inside EPS; band_position carries no information.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 86.18-111.16
data_sources.financials: PNW_Metrics.csv (SEC XBRL, FY2008-FY2025 and quarters to Q3-2026); Q3-2026 10-Q for share count, forward sale agreements, convertible notes, debt, equity, dividends declared and the Nuclear PTC position
data_sources.qualitative: PNW_Analysis.json (2026-11-15) for guidance, rate-case status, ACC election result and bull/bear axes
